description: LuMod is a public Python package and GitLab code repository of lumped rainfall-runoff models. Its README names MILC, HYMOD, HBV, GR4J, GR2M and GR1A, with daily, monthly or annual time steps depending on the model, plus tools for parameter calibration and uncertainty analysis. PyPI lists version 0.1.3.0, and the repository's licence file states GNU GPL version 3; the software is free to obtain. Users supply catchment area, coordinates, meteorological forcing and model parameters, then obtain simulated flow and other water-balance outputs. The models can test reservoir inflow, drought and water-supply scenarios where a lumped catchment representation is suitable. A limitation is that lumping obscures within-basin spatial variation and local infrastructure detail. The inspected GitLab project shows last activity in 2022, so compatibility with current Python dependencies should be tested before use. It relates to model-smhi-hype-hydrological-model as a separate catchment modelling family. The cited article used LuMod for SSP-CABra simulations; no code was executed here.
